deep.reconstruction:
This page is not mathematics. It is part of Gauss's postal register (Briefjournal) for 1815, covering January, February and the start of March. The headings are 'Von' (letters received) and 'An' (letters sent). Each line gives a date and a correspondent: Olbers, Wachter, (von) Lindenau, Gerling, Möbius, Fraunhofer, Repsold, Bode, Bessel, Fleischer, Nicolai, Spengler, v. Zimmermann, v. Arnswald, the Curatorium (Göttingen university administration) and Mathiessen. Braces group letters that went together in one packet or were charged once.

The ruled columns on the right record postage. The next page's header names two currency accounts, 'Convent.' and 'Cassen'.
- The left group has three subcolumns. Only the Fraunhofer (Munich) letter of Jan 9 ('— 3 —') and the Fleischer letter of Feb 27 ('— 14 —') use it.
- The right group is in groschen and pfennige, with 12 pf = 1 gr.

Monthly totals:
- January. Letters received, counted from the page: Lindenau, Gerling, Möbius, Lindenau, Olbers, Fraunhofer, Repsold, v. Lindenau, v. Lindenau, Gerling, Olbers = 11, as Gauss writes. Letters sent: Gauss writes 8.
- January postage, right group. Groschen: 3 (Olbers) + 1 (Hannover) + 3 (Fraunhofer) + 3 (Olbers) = 10 gr. Pfennige: 2+2+2+2+2+6+2+2+6+2+2 = 30 pf = 2 gr 6 pf. Total 12 gr 6 pf, matching 'Januar ... 12 6'. Left group total 3.
- February. Received: Nicolai, Spengler, v. Zimmermann, v. Lindenau, Curatorium, Nicolai, von Lindenau, Fleischer = 8. Sent: Bode, Bessel, Möbius, Fleischer, Nicolai, v. Arnswald, Repsold, v. Lindenau, Gerling, Spengler = 10. Both match Gauss's figures.
- February postage, right group. Groschen: 6+8+3+3+1 = 21. Pfennige: 3+2+2+2+8+2+6+2 = 27 = 2 gr 3 pf. Total 23 gr 3 pf, matching '23 3'. Left group 14, from Fleischer.
- March begins: Bessel, v. Lindenau and Gerling received on the 2nd, bracketed, 4 pf; a letter to von Lindenau; Mathiessen on the 3rd, 2 pf.

The previous page, a frequency/cumulative-sum table, is unrelated. The only 'mathematics' here is bookkeeping arithmetic with mixed units, and the monthly sums check out.
errors: January 'An' count: the image lists 9 sent entries (Olbers, Wachter, Lindenau, Olbers, '(nach Hannover)' on the 12th, Olbers on the 15th, v. Lindenau, Fraunhofer, v. Lindenau), but Gauss writes 8. Most likely the '(nach Hannover)' line of the 12th and the Olbers letter of the 15th are one item, or the Hannover line is a routing note. This is not an arithmetic error.
All postage totals checked (Jan 12 gr 6 pf, Feb 23 gr 3 pf, left-column totals 3 and 14) are correct.

results.what: Monthly tally of letters received and sent and of postage in groschen/pfennige (12 pf = 1 gr), for Gauss's correspondence of Jan–Mar 1815
results.usually_credited_to: n/a (Gauss's own Briefjournal; used by editors of the Gauss correspondence)

deep.surprise_reason: This is an administrative postage and correspondence log with routine sums. Gauss's correspondents in 1815 are well documented, so it holds nothing mathematically novel. Its value is purely biographical and archival, for dating letters.

checkable.asserts: January postage sums to 12 gr 6 pf
February postage sums to 23 gr 3 pf

transcription_corrections: Jan 12 line: in the left (Convent.) group a struck-out entry '4 6' (or '+ 6'); the charge is entered in the right group as '1 6'.
Jan 30 v. Lindenau: postage '— 2' belongs in the right group (0 gr 2 pf).
Feb 9 Nicolai/v. Arnswald: the shared charge is '3 8' in the right group; the '—' on the Nicolai line is a placeholder.
Mar 2 bracket (Bessel, v. Lindenau, Gerling): postage '— 4', i.e. 0 gr 4 pf.
Mar 3 Mathiessen: the date is corrected to 3 (overwritten), postage '— 2'.
